state.error: An error occurred. Applies to paused torrents.
state.uploading: Torrent is seeding and data is being uploaded.
state.pausedUP: Torrent is paused and has finished downloading.
state.stoppedUP: Torrent is stopped and has finished downloading.
state.queuedUP: Queuing is enabled and torrent is queued for upload.
state.stalledUP: Torrent is seeding, but no connections were made.
state.checkingUP: Torrent has finished downloading and is being checked.
state.forcedUP: Torrent is forced to upload and ignores queue limits.
state.allocating: Torrent is allocating disk space for download.
state.downloading: Torrent is downloading and data is being transferred.
state.metaDL: Torrent has started and is fetching metadata.
state.pausedDL: Torrent is paused and has not finished downloading.
state.stoppedDL: Torrent is stopped and has not finished downloading.
state.queuedDL: Queuing is enabled and torrent is queued for download.
state.stalledDL: Torrent is downloading, but no connections were made.
state.checkingDL: Torrent is being checked and has not finished downloading.
state.forcedDL: Torrent is forced to download and ignores queue limits.
state.checkingResumeData: Checking resume data on qBittorrent startup.
state.moving: Torrent is being moved to another location.

about.tagline: The digital butler for your torrents
about.description: BitButler is a modern cross-platform desktop client for managing qBittorrent servers remotely. Built with Angular and Electron.

add-form.paused: Add torrents in the paused state

description.line1: Controls whether the torrent's files are nested inside a main folder or placed directly in the download path.
description.line2: Default (unset): Uses the global setting defined in your qBittorrent options.
description.line3: Create root folder: Forces the creation of a containing folder (based on the torrent's name) inside your download directory.
description.line4: Do not create root folder: Places the contents directly into the download directory. This is useful for single-file torrents to avoid unnecessary subfolders.

description.line1: Normally, qBittorrent verifies existing data on your disk to ensure it matches the torrent perfectly. Enabling this skips that scan.
description.line2: Use this only if you are 100% sure the files in your "Save Path" are already complete and uncorrupted; otherwise, you risk uploading "garbage" data to others.

description.line1: The torrent will appear in your list but won't start downloading or uploading until you manually hit "Resume".
description.line2: This is great if you want to add a bunch of files now but wait for off-peak hours to start the actual traffic.

description.line1: When enabled, qBittorrent handles the file location based on the Category you assign.
description.line2: For example, if you change a torrent's category from "Movies" to "TV", the software will automatically move the files to the corresponding folder on your hard drive.

description.line1: Torrents usually download pieces in a random order based on what is available. This option forces it to download from the beginning of the file to the end.
description.line2: It's useful if you want to preview/stream a video file while it is still downloading, though it can sometimes slow down the overall download speed.

description.line1: This tells the client to grab the very first and very last chunks of the file immediately.
description.line2: This is helpful for verifying that a file is valid or for certain media players to read the file headers and metadata (like duration and resolution) before the rest of the file arrives.

description.line1: Sets the display name and the root folder name for this torrent.
description.line2: This does not affect the filenames inside the torrent - only the display name and the root folder name (if a root folder is created).

description.line1: Select a .torrent file from your computer. The file will be parsed locally - no data is sent anywhere until you click Add.
description.line2: Once a file is loaded, a file tree will appear below so you can review and toggle individual files before adding.

description.line1: Paste one or more magnet links or direct .torrent URLs here, one per line.
description.line2: Magnet links start with magnet:?xt=urn:btih:… - direct .torrent URLs point to a remote file that qBittorrent will fetch automatically.

description.line1: Assigns the torrent to a category. Categories are useful for organizing your downloads and can also define a default save path.

time-active.description: Total duration this torrent has been running in the client.

eta.title: ETA
eta.description: Estimated time remaining until the download is complete based on current speed.

connections.title: Connections
connections.description: Number of active connections to peers out of the total limit for this torrent.

downloaded.title: Downloaded
downloaded.description: Total amount of data successfully downloaded for this torrent.

uploaded.title: Uploaded
uploaded.description: Total amount of data you have shared with other peers.

seeds.title: Seeds
seeds.description: The number of users currently connected who have 100% of the file.

download-speed.title: Download Speed
download-speed.description: The current rate at which you are receiving data.

upload-speed.title: Upload Speed
upload-speed.description: The current rate at which you are sending data to others.

peers.title: Peers
peers.description: Users who are currently downloading the file (leechers) and have only parts of it.

download-limit.title: Download Limit
download-limit.description: The maximum allowed speed for downloading this torrent.

upload-limit.title: Upload Limit
upload-limit.description: The maximum allowed speed for uploading this torrent.

wasted.title: Wasted
wasted.description: Data that was discarded due to corruption or hash failures.

share-ratio.title: Share Ratio
share-ratio.description: The ratio of uploaded data to downloaded data (Uploaded / Downloaded).

reannounce-in.title: Reannounce In
reannounce-in.description: Time remaining until the client requests an updated peer list from the tracker.

last-seen-complete.title: Last Seen Complete
last-seen-complete.description: The last time this client was connected to a peer with 100% of the file.

ratio-limit.title: Ratio Limit
ratio-limit.description: The upload/download ratio at which this torrent will stop seeding.

seeding-time-limit.title: Seeding Time Limit
seeding-time-limit.description: How long (in minutes) this torrent will keep seeding after it completes.

inactive-seeding-time-limit.title: Inactive Seeding Time Limit
inactive-seeding-time-limit.description: How long (in minutes) this torrent may remain idle while seeding before it is stopped.

total-size.title: Total Size
total-size.description: The full size of all files included in this torrent.

pieces.title: Pieces
pieces.description: The total number of data chunks the file is divided into and how many you currently possess.

created-by.title: Created By
created-by.description: The application or user agent that originally created the .torrent file.

added-on.title: Added On
added-on.description: The date and time this torrent was added to your client.

completed-on.title: Completed On
completed-on.description: The date and time when the download reached 100%.

created-on.title: Created On
created-on.description: The date and time the .torrent file was originally generated.

info-hash-v1.title: Info Hash v1
info-hash-v1.description: The unique SHA-1 identifier for this torrent.

info-hash-v2.title: Info Hash v2
info-hash-v2.description: The unique SHA-256 identifier for BitTorrent v2 compatible torrents.

comment.title: Comment
comment.description: Optional text added by the torrent creator, often containing source info or credits.

loading.title: Loading...
loading.message: Connecting to qBittorrent and syncing torrent peers

D.label: Downloading
D.description: You are currently receiving data from this peer.

U.label: Uploading
U.description: You are currently sending data to this peer.

d.label: Interested (Down)
d.description: You want to download from them, but they are choking you (refusing to send).

u.label: Interested (Up)
u.description: They want to download from you, but you are choking them.

O.label: Optimistic Unchoke
O.description: You are testing this peer to see if they give you good speeds.

S.label: Snubbed
S.description: The peer hasn't sent you data for a while, so you've stopped sending to them.

I.label: Incoming
I.description: The peer connected to you (useful for checking if your ports are open).

E.label: Encrypted
E.description: The connection is using protocol encryption.

H.label: DHT
H.description: Found via Distributed Hash Table (no tracker needed).

X.label: PEX
X.description: Found via Peer Exchange (other peers told you about them).

L.label: Local
L.description: Found via Local Peer Discovery (same Wi-Fi/LAN).

P.label: uTP
P.description: The connection is using the Micro Transport Protocol (UDP-based).

api-polling.description: BitButler is using API polling to get the current state of the torrents in your list. Here you can configure how frequent this polling should occur.

foreground-polling.description: The polling frequency when the application is open.

description.line2: This way you can open local paths in the operating systems native file browser from the Torrent Details view, or if configured, from the torrent list view.

warning.too-low-polling-frequency: Setting this value too low may cause problems.

status-bar.title: Status Bar
status-bar.description: Configure the visibility and order of available widgets in the status bar at the bottom. Drag and drop widgets to enable, disable, or reorder them.

animate-rows.title: Torrent List Animations
animate-rows.description: There is an animation on the torrent list whenever a row is changing. If you face any performance issues, you may want to turn this off.

pagination.title: Torrent List Pagination
pagination.description: The torrent list can be set to use pagination. Having too many torrents in your list may impact performance. If you have issues, you may try enabling pagination.

compact-rows.title: Compact Rows
compact-rows.description: Reduces the row height and cell padding in the torrent list for a denser view.

floating-filters.title: Floating Filters
floating-filters.description: Shows an inline filter row beneath the column headers. This can also be toggled per-column from the column header context menu.

double-click-behavior.title: Double Click Behavior
double-click-behavior.description: The rows in the torrent list can be double clicked. The action taken by BitButler can be:
double-click-behavior.list-item-1:
Show in Folder / Open Destination: For single-file torrents: Opens the destination folder and selects the file. For multi-file torrents: Opens the destination folder.
This feature requires Path Mappings to be configured in your server settings.
double-click-behavior.list-item-2: Open Torrent Details: opening the torrent details view

column-order.title: Ordering Columns
column-order.description: Here you can configure the order of the enabled columns in the torrent list.

column-pool.title: Column Pool
column-pool.description: Here you can enable / disable the columns visible in your torrent list.

bandwidth.description: Configure download and upload speed limits, alternative rate limits for Turtle Mode, and a time-based speed scheduler.

hint.global-rate-limits: Sets the maximum combined download and upload speed across all torrents. Enter 0 for unlimited.
hint.alt-rate-limits: Throttled speed limits used when Turtle Mode is manually enabled or activated by the scheduler.
hint.scheduler: Automatically switches to alternative rate limits during a configured time window on selected days.
